scope.description: Check the local participant-eligibility relation from verification registration through support aggregation and quorum notification. Use three voters, including the local leader, and one nonvoter. After registration, deliver positive support only from the nonvoter and observe whether it satisfies the threshold. Compare with an otherwise identical case delivering support from one remote voter.
assumptions: Latest and committed configurations agree and remain unchanged throughout the check.
The local server is a voter in an initialized leader episode.
Replication workers correspond to the configured remote server identities.
Each controlled positive notification represents one successful append response for its identified worker.
The fixture establishes the local entry state; it does not establish a complete election or partition history.
excluded: Proof of an election or partition history producing stale leadership
Configuration changes, worker retirement, and suffrage changes during verification
Ordering between verification completion, negative support, and pending step-down
Proof of stale FSM reads, incorrect commitment, or client-visible data loss

properties.reason: Actual result fields are compared after independent prerequisite association

adaptations: Construct only the leader state, stable configuration, worker maps, and channels consumed by the selected methods; do not run an election, replication goroutines, or the main leader loop.
Invoke the actual worker notifyAll(true) method at the accepted successful-response notification boundary. The positive input is controlled; no network response is claimed to have been observed.
Use a capacity-one verification channel instead of a concurrent main-loop receiver. This changes notification blocking, while retaining actual registration, counting, locking, and notification logic.
Observe quorum notification after notifyAll returns; do not synthesize future completion or claim a public VerifyLeader return.
boundaries: Proof of an election or partition history producing stale leadership
Configuration changes, worker retirement, and suffrage changes during verification
Ordering between verification completion, negative support, and pending step-down
Proof of stale FSM reads, incorrect commitment, or client-visible data loss
Controlled boolean support represents the accepted response-notification boundary; the harness does not observe an actual AppendEntries exchange.
The requirement's voter-only applicability is derived from the supplied interface responsibilities and selected quorum mechanism.
Notification and externally effective VerifyLeader completion are distinct endpoints.
Election history, response freshness, membership transitions, pending step-down ordering, lease timing, and client consequences remain outside the measured comparison.

The normative basis remains the explicitly attributed relationship among leadership assurance, declared suffrage and the voter-derived threshold; the API does not expressly prescribe VerifyLeader voter eligibility.

The fixture establishes consumed local state and injects positive support. It does not demonstrate an election history, an actual AppendEntries exchange or distributed reachability of a stale-leader execution.
The observations establish a local eligibility discrepancy, not public VerifyLeader completion, lost leadership, a stale read, incorrect commitment or data loss.
Response freshness, membership transitions, worker retirement, concurrent negative support, pending step-down and lease timing remain outside this check.
The supplied observations demonstrate both concrete comparison cases; they do not establish broader schedule coverage or production exposure.
